title: Cases of Foreign Domestic Workers Borrowing and Defaulting on Loans from Licensed and Unlicensed Moneylenders
what_it_is: Cases of Foreign Domestic Workers Borrowing and Defaulting on Loans from Licensed and Unlicensed Moneylenders

sections.label: Work pass revoked for unlicensed borrowing
sections.summary: MOM announced that work pass holders who borrow from unlicensed moneylenders will have their passes revoked, be repatriated and debarred, with the rule implemented in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To send a clear signal of our strong stand, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) had earlier announced that if a work pass holder is found to have borrowed from unlicensed moneylenders, the employer will be informed and the employee's work pass revoked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The foreign worker will then be repatriated and debarred from further employment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The rule against borrowing from unlicensed moneylenders will be implemented in 2019, following a period of education and communication with work pass holders and their employers.

sections.label: FDW loans from licensed moneylenders
sections.summary: The number of FDWs who took loans from licensed moneylenders was about 1,500 in 2016, 12,000 in 2017 and 28,000 in the first half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The number of FDWs who took loans from licensed moneylenders was approximately 1,500 in 2016, 12,000 in 2017 and 28,000 in the first half of 2018.

sections.label: MinLaw measures on foreigner over-borrowing
sections.summary: On 4 October 2018, MinLaw announced two measures to strengthen protections for FDWs and other foreigners in Singapore from over-borrowing, following a rise in foreigner borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In view of the recent increase in foreigners borrowing from moneylenders, on 4 October 2018, MinLaw announced two measures to strengthen protections for FDWs and other foreigners residing in Singapore from the effects of over-borrowing.

sections.label: Lower loan cap for low earners
sections.summary: There will be a lower cap of $1,500 for all foreigners residing in Singapore who earn less than $10,000 annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, there will also be a lower cap of $1,500 for all foreigners residing in Singapore who earn less than $10,000 annually.

sections.label: FDWs borrowing for home needs
sections.summary: Anecdotal evidence shows that in some cases FDWs borrow from licensed moneylenders to meet requests from home, such as unforeseen medical bills or children's college fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Anecdotal evidence tells us that, in certain cases, FDWs borrow from the licensed moneylenders to tide through certain requests from home, such as unforeseen medical bills, college fees for their children and so on.

sections.label: Educating FDWs on licensed moneylenders
sections.summary: First, education efforts will be intensified to help FDWs understand who the licensed and unlicensed moneylenders are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: First, we will intensify the education efforts to help FDW understand who are the licensed vis-à-vis the unlicensed moneylenders.
